text:
maria: Heads up — saw a sharp drop in prefix cache hit-rate on prod A around 09:12 UTC after the kernel-priority reorder and the batching_coalesce toggle went out. Latencies spiked ~2.3x for small-chat requests.

devon: seeing it too. prefix_hitrate went from ~0.28 to 0.004 in 3 minutes. affecting rack-4 and rack-7 primarily.

alex: timeline? which deploy included the kernel priority change vs batching flag?

maria: deploy 2098765400 rolled kernel-selector v2 (we bumped AVX512-optimized kernel to higher priority) and at 2098765420 we toggled batching_coalesce=true for aggressive coalescing.

hao: quick profiling shows per-request working set >4x when AVX512 kernel selected (more temp buffers). that increases KV pressure. suspect combined effect: bigger runtime footprint + bigger batches = faster eviction of prefix entries.

peggy: can you paste the hotspot metrics?

hao: paste from the perf probe:
```
metric prefix_hitrate 09:10 0.28
metric prefix_hitrate 09:13 0.004
metric kv_evictions/s 09:10 12
metric kv_evictions/s 09:13 420
metric avg_latency_small_chat_ms 09:10 42
metric avg_latency_small_chat_ms 09:13 98
kernel_choice: AVX512 -> % selected 09:10 12% -> 88% 09:13
batching_coalesce: false -> true at 09:12
```

devon: omg kv_evictions jumped so hard. any tenant-specific noisy behavior?

maria: early signals point to tenant:content-psi sending a high fraction of long-context requests concurrently. their prefix cardinality is huge.

ops: paging infra oncall — should we revert batching_coalesce first or the kernel priority? which is safer?

alex: revert batching_coalesce=true first — less risky for model correctness, and it should reduce transient working set pressure quickly.

maria: rolling rollback of batching_coalesce to false on prod A starting. will monitor.

sre-bot: deploy rollback started: cfg-batching_coalesce revert by maria @ 09:18 UTC -> job 4821.

devon: after rollback, prefix_hitrate recovering slowly: 0.004 -> 0.06 in 4 minutes. evictions down to ~60/s.

hao: still higher than baseline. kernel still selects AVX512 heavily; memory footprint still elevated. we need longer-term: either throttle kernel priority autoselect or add a working-set guard for KV.

peggy: can we add a soft cap per-tenant on KV entries until post-deploy stabilization?

alex: yes, add a per-tenant eviction-reserve and prefer LRU across tenants. Also add metric that correlates kernel_choice -> per-request mem delta.

maria: did a quick hotfix: added temporary tenant_cap=2000 for content-psi on prod A. will keep for 30m.

ops: content-psi traffic dipped a bit after cap, hit-rate improved further to 0.12 and p50 latency down to 55ms.

devon: root cause summary for the incident thread: kernel-priority reorder increased selection of a higher-memory AVX512 kernel; batching_coalesce toggle increased coalesced batch sizes; together these changed working set and triggered tenant-focused KV eviction storms, causing prefix hit-rate collapse and latency spike.

hao: follow-ups: 1) limit kernel priority weight when mem footprint delta > X, 2) add batching_coalesce safety check tied to working_set_pressure, 3) implement per-tenant KV reservation and telemetry, 4) replay test with a noisy-tenant synthetic workload.

peggy: I'll own 3) and 4). devon + hao take 1) and 2).

maria: logging: created incident doc https://go.redwood/incident/2098765432 and added initial notes.

ops: closing the immediate alert, leaving incident open for follow-ups. thanks all :thumbsup:

alex: small note — we should also add a regression test in the kernel selector that runs a 'kv-pressure' scenario on each candidate before promoting priority. prevents similar surprises.

devon: agreed. adding to the release checklist.

sre-bot: incident severity lowered to P3 at 09:42 UTC.

maria: final status: prefix_hitrate back to 0.21 on prod A, avg small-chat latency within SLO. follow-ups assigned.

peggy: will file a design doc for per-tenant reservation and add perf sims.

hao: posting the small profiling snippet saved: `pmap --summary` showed 3.2GB -> 13GB process delta when AVX512 kernel used with big-coalesced batches — that's an easy guard rule.

devon: thanks team.
